about: One script for both of a replica's syncs: the browser's FennecSync (web/fennec.js, run by web/fennec.sync.scenarios.test.js) and the native core every binding drives (crates/fennec-abi/src/sync, run by crates/fennec-abi/tests/scenarios.rs).

A scenario starts with no replica and plays its steps in order. `do` says what happens: start, restart (the app opened again over the replica it kept; either with `token`, the token it starts with, null for none, t0 unless given), seed / change (a stream event of the shape at index `shape`, 0 by default), error (the stream's error event, its `error`, `status` and `code`), drop (every stream ends), fire (every timer asked for runs out), answer (the oldest write request not yet answered gets `status`, `seq` as Fennec-Seq and `body`; status 0 is no answer at all), write (an app's write: insert / insert_new (the builders' insertNew, FennecQL's insert) / update / delete / upsert / batch, a value {"$inc": n} as inc(n) and {"$expr": text} as expr(text), and get, a read with its require, in a batch; `require` and `reason` as the builders' { require: n, reason }; text, a FennecQL text and its `params` as an app runs it on the replica itself -- a native binding's run, the browser's db.local.query -- never in a batch, and here only one the replica refuses whole), net (whether the server is reached: a stream or GET /collections made while it is not fails at once), stream_status (the next stream opened is answered with its `status` and `body`, {"error":"refused"} unless given; `held`, only at the next release, the request still out meanwhile), schema_status (the same for the next GET /collections), release (every answer held is given, in the order held), online (the platform's network signal), token (a token handed over, the same one again among them: the answer of the provider's call out where one is, the app's own handover otherwise), set_token (the app's own token while the provider's call stays out -- a provider that never returns: the core told {"token":..}, the page's setToken; a later token or token_failed step is that call's answer, which answers the ask out then), token_failed (the provider asked threw `error`, or handed over none: the core told {"token_failed":error}), stop (the replica stopped: the core told {"stop":true}, the page's FennecSync closed), schema (what GET /collections answers from now on). One ask for a token is out at a time: a runner fails a scenario whose sync asks again before the ask out was answered. A provider is called once at a time, as every binding calls it: an ask made while its call is out calls it no second time, and is that call's to answer.

After each step the runner checks `expect`: requests (the GETs and POSTs made during the step: method, path, auth, key = the Idempotency-Key, body = the lines sent, lines = how many), streams (each stream opened: its path and query, auth), rows (the replica's rows of a collection by id, each row's named fields), pending (writes not yet answered), refused (each write refused, as it was told: a status alone is one told with no quota, {status, quota} one a tenant's quota refused, {status, reason} one a require's reason refused), quota (the tenant's quota the status's last error names, null for none), code (the code the status's last error names, token_expired where the server said the token's exp passed, null for none: FennecSync's errorCode), token_asked, token (what the provider was handed during the step, null where it was not called -- an ask made while its call is out calls it no second time: its code, had_token -- whether the refused request carried a token -- and attempt, the asks in a row since the server last took the token held, an expiry of another token than the last one refused for its expiry starting it at 1 again; the core's token action, FennecSync's TokenRefusal as errorCode, hadToken and attempt, whose expired is always its code's), token_wait (what the status says of the token the sync waits on, null where it waits on none: its stage -- delayed while the wait before the next ask runs, asked once the provider, or an app handing its tokens over itself, is asked and has not answered, failed where the provider threw or handed over none -- and the code, had_token and attempt the ask said, or delayed will say; said from where the ask stands, so nothing failing since, a stream ending among them, hides it: the core's status token, FennecSync's status().token as its stage and its refusal's errorCode, hadToken and attempt), status_error (a text the status's error says, null for none, the token's while one is wanted: the core's status error's message, FennecSync's status().error), waits (each timer asked for, [min, max] ms), ready (every shape seeded), error (a start or a write refused before anything is sent), reason (the reason that error gave, a require's).

An object expected is a subset of the one that came; a list is whole. A string `<name>` is any value, the same wherever the name comes again and another than every other name's: a key made for an insert, an Idempotency-Key. In a step's data a bound `<name>` stands for its value, so the server's copy of a row carries the key the app made. `@name` in rows or puts is a fixture.

Writes are written with their fields in alphabetical order, as the builders render them in the order given: JavaScript keeps an object's order and the native runner's JSON sorts it. A temporary id is 2^52 = 4503599627370496 and up.

Where the platforms differ on purpose a scenario says why in `differs`, and a step's expect_js / expect_native hold each side's own. Both runners write the names that passed to target/sync-scenarios/, and integrations/sync-scenarios-check.mjs fails unless both ran every one.
